results.title: CLOGSAG demands probe into alleged assault on Okaikwei North Assembly worker
results.content: The Civil and Local Government Staff Association of Ghana (CLOGSAG) has called for a full-scale investigation into the alleged slapping of an administrative officer of the Okaikwei North Municipal Assembly, warning that violence against public servants cannot be tolerated in the workplace.

results.title: Twifo Praso clash: One dead, police deploy 100 officers after anti-drug raid
results.content: A police operation targeting suspected drug hideouts at Twifo Praso in the Central Region has ended in violence, leaving one civilian dead, several others injured, and three police officers hurt.

results.title: Kosmos Energy renovates dining hall at Senya SHS
results.content: Kosmos Energy Ghana (KEG) has renovated the dining hall at Senya Senior High School in the Awutu Senya District of the Central Region, providing dining furniture and kitchen facilities to serve about 800 students. The project followed the completion and handover of a school clinic to the institution in February 2025. Subsequent engagements with school authorities identified the poor condition of the dining hall and the need to improve facilities for students and kitchen staff.

results.title: Twice billed for dirty state databases
results.content: At 2:26 pm on 24 November 2026, a speed camera flashed along a northern highway. A commercial minivan wearing a 2026 Greater Accra plate, GT [REDACTED]-26, clocked 85 km/h in a 50 km/h zone. Hours later, Police MTTD dispatched a GH¢240.00 speeding ticket through TraffiTech-GH.

results.title: Budget projections vulnerable to global and domestic shocks — Terkper
results.content: Former Finance Minister Seth Terkper has cautioned against judging government budget projections without considering the economic shocks that can undermine revenue and expenditure assumptions after the estimates have been prepared.

results.title: Leroy Botchey named HR Future Leader Under 35
results.content: A Human Resource professional and HR Administration Manager at Société Générale Ghana PLC, Leroy Botchey was named the HR Future Leader Under 35 Award recipient at the 2026 HR Professionals Summit & Awards in Accra.

results.title: Opportunity International Savings and Loans pays courtesy call on Ga Mantse
results.content: Opportunity International Savings and Loans Ltd. (Opportunity) paid a courtesy call on King Tackie Teiko Tsuru II, the Ga Mantse, to deepen its partnership with the Ga Traditional Council and foster collaboration to support socio-economic development in the Ga traditional area.

results.title: Accra Mall celebrates Ghanaian music through Homegrown Stars
results.content: A Saturday shopping trip can easily turn into a full day out with good food, great company, and a little entertainment along the way. That was the experience for visitors to Accra Mall over the weekend as Homegrown Stars brought Ghanaian music into the weekend atmosphere.

results.title: Past debt obligations complicate government’s spending decisions – Terkper
results.content: Presidential Advisor on the Economy, Seth Terkper, says inherited debt obligations and economic uncertainties are complicating the government’s spending decisions amid concerns over budgetary cuts.

results.title: ‘No more borrowing after HIPC and defaults’ — Seth Terkper
results.content: Former Finance Minister Seth Terkper has urged successive governments to exercise lasting fiscal discipline and resist the temptation to accumulate unsustainable debt, warning that Ghana must not repeat the borrowing practices that led to its debt crisis.

results.title: The Glorified Destitute: How vanity is bankrupting a generation
results.content: We have perfected the stupidity of looking wealthy while being financially bankrupt. Across Ghana, people would rather impress strangers than secure their own futures. A man earning GH₵8,000 a month will impoverish himself to acquire a GH₵200,000 status symbol. A depreciating piece of metal that consumes money in fuel, maintenance and repairs while steadily losing value. He cannot build an asset, but he must drive an expensive car. He cannot afford financial independence, but he must look successful. We have become addicted to the appearance of wealth and allergic to the discipline required to create it. Nowhere is this national affliction more embarrassing than in our politics.

results.title: Government cannot escape financial obligations of previous administration – Terkper
results.content: Presidential Advisor on the Economy, Seth Terkper, says the government cannot escape financial obligations inherited from previous administrations, even as ministries and agencies mount pressure over budgetary allocations.

results.content: The Head of Communications for Regal Film Festival and Awards (REFFA), Kpekpo Maxwell Justice (KMJ), has highlighted how the scheme is changing the face of Ghana’s movie industry.

results.content: Two Italian nationals have died following a strike on a facility in Kuwait which both countries have blamed on Iran.

results.content: Seth Terkper, Presidential Advisor on the Economy, has revisited the controversy over cocoa producer prices, questioning the sector's apparent silence as economic pressures mount.

results.content: Volodymyr Zelensky has voiced deep frustration with the US, saying that delays in delivering vital anti-ballistic missiles are costing Ukrainian lives and complaining that the US is not pushing Russia hard enough during peace talks.

results.content: Dinese Jackson couldn't ​stomach spending roughly $1,500 to fly herself and her two children from Raleigh, North Carolina, to Dallas, Texas, for Thanksgiving, more than double what she had paid for similar trips ‌in the past.

results.title: Trump’s newest order curtailing birthright citizenship is blocked by second judge
results.content: A second US judge on Wednesday blocked enforcement of President Donald Trump's executive ​order limiting the number of people eligible for birthright citizenship, which Trump signed after the US Supreme Court rejected ‌his initial effort to impose restrictions.

results.title: Four injured as tanker, medicine truck and passenger vehicle crash on Fumesua-Ejisu Road
results.content: Four people have been injured in a three-vehicle collision involving a fuel tanker, a truck carrying medicines for Shalom Pharmacy Limited and a passenger Ford vehicle on the Fumesua-Ejisu Road in the Ashanti Region.

results.title: Gold rebounds from one-year low as AI jitters ease
results.content: Gold prices rose Friday, rebounding from a more-than-one-year low touched earlier this week as a US holiday lull calmed AI-driven market jitters and eased selling pressure on bullion.

results.title: Government pays GH¢12.9bn to DDEP bondholders ahead of 2027 maturity
results.content: The government has paid GH¢12.89 billion to investors who accepted its offer to cash out of bonds due in February 2027, bringing forward the settlement of nearly half of the outstanding securities by several months.

results.title: The American manager with a maths degree making history in La Liga
results.content: From kicking a ball around New Jersey parks to lifting the Copa del Rey with Real Sociedad, Pellegrino Matarazzo's journey to managing the La Liga side has been anything but conventional.

results.title: Ten-man Bournemouth beat Celta Vigo for 10th win in row
results.content: Ten-man Bournemouth came from behind to beat Celta Vigo in the Europa League, extending their club-record winning run to 10 games.

results.title: Falling cocoa prices: Terkper questions silence after last year’s fierce debate
results.content: Presidential Advisor on the Economy, Seth Terkper, has questioned the apparent silence on falling cocoa prices after last year's intense public debate over payments to cocoa farmers during last year’s budget discussions.

results.title: Youth groups take over Accra streets to show life beyond cars using fossil fuels
results.content: Youth-led mobility groups are calling for Accra's streets to be redesigned for people and not just cars. They have been closing sections of road to traffic and handing them over to walkers, cyclists and children at play. The initiative, called the Open Street Fair, is organised by Transform Transport Accra, UrbanBetter Accra Cityzens and Global Shapers Accra, with support from the United Nation Environment Programme (UNEP), WALK21 Foundation, and the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). The groups say they want residents to experience cleaner, safer ways of getting around and to see for themselves that these alternatives are possible. results.title: Youth run through Airport Residential Area to map Accra’s polluted air
results.content: A youth-led run through Accra’s Airport Residential Area has recorded elevated levels of fine particulate matter, with average PM2.5 concentrations more than three times the World Health Organization’s recommended daily guideline. The 5.3-kilometre exercise, organised by Breathe Cities Accra and youth and transport advocacy groups, used portable air quality sensors to measure pollution along streets in the neighbourhood. The run began at 6:30am on Wednesday, November 25, from the African Regent Hotel under the theme, “Breathe Accra: Reclaiming our streets for cleaner air, one run at a time.” It brought together Breathe Cities Accra, UrbanBetter Accra Cityzens, Global Shapers Accra, Transform Transport Accra and the Green Africa Youth Organisation.

results.title: Stakeholders in the Bono East region call for collective action as terrorism threat nears Ghana’s borders
results.content: In a significant move to strengthen Ghana's defenses against evolving security threats in West Africa, a three-day stakeholder engagement and public forum has been held to review the National Framework for Preventing and Countering Violent Extremism and Terrorism (NAFPCVET) in the Bono East Region.

results.title: MDPI urges public and private institutions to prioritise staff training ahead of 2027
results.content: The Management Development and Productivity Institute (MDPI) is urging public and private sector institutions to prioritise staff training and capacity building as part of efforts to improve productivity and support Ghana’s economic transformation agenda. Director-General of MDPI, Prof. Elijah Yendaw, says strengthening the capacity of managers and employees is critical to improving institutional performance and ensuring the effective implementation of government policies and programmes. Speaking at an MDPI CEO Breakfast Meeting, he said the institute was engaging various organisations to identify their training needs and develop targeted capacity-building programmes ahead of 2027. results.title: GIISDEC targets submission of iron and steel industry regulations to Parliament in three months
results.content: The Ghana Integrated Iron and Steel Development Corporation (GIISDEC) is targeting the submission of a proposed Legislative Instrument (LI) to Parliament within the next two to three months to regulate Ghana’s iron and steel industry. The proposed regulation is expected to establish guidelines for activities across the upstream, midstream and downstream segments of the industry, including the scrap metal sector. GIISDEC Chief Executive Officer, William Okofo Dartey, disclosed this at a stakeholders’ consultation forum in Accra on Thursday, November 26, 2026. He said the consultation forms part of efforts to operationalise the Ghana Integrated Iron and Steel Development Corporation Act, 2019 (Act 988), and is intended to gather contributions from industry players and government agencies before the proposed LI is finalised.
